messages:

Subject: Partner claim lifecycle & handback proposal

Team,

Uploading a concise proposal for how we treat partner account claims when territory overlap occurs and how we handback accounts cleanly if the partner drops out of a deal. Goal: reduce friction for sellers, avoid duplicated outreach, and create a predictable handback SLA for partners + Redwood.

TL;DR proposal (attached: claim-matrix-v1.xlsx, map-diagram.png):
- Claim lifecycle states: Claimed -> Active -> Escrowed -> Handback -> Closed.
- Primary owner during Active = claimant partner. During Escrowed, we freeze outbound co-sell motions and set a 30-day activity window.
- Handback triggers: 30 days with no logged activity from partner OR formal withdrawal request. Handback notification -> 7-day seller objection window -> auto-handback.
- Escrow: If a seller contests within 7 days, move to Escrowed and attempt rapid mediation (Partner Ops + AE) for up to 21 days. If unresolved, handback to owner of record.
- Documentation: partner must supply cold call evidence and opportunity owner notes to maintain Active status.

Operational asks:
1) Ops: confirm event flags (partner_activity, seller_objection) to drive automation.
2) Sales: confirm 30-day SLA vs 21-day suggestion (I prefer 30 but open).
3) Legal/Partnership: any carve-outs for reseller or OEM deals?

Please review the attached claim matrix; the diagram shows how account tags move between partner pools. If we agree on the mechanics, I'll circulate a one-page playbook for sellers and partners.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Head of Alliances | Redwood Inference

Karthik — thanks for pulling this together. High-level: +1 on the lifecycle states, very helpful. A few quick notes inline and a couple asks below.

Inline:
- Handback SLA: I suggest 21 days for handback after Escrow if activity is nil. Shorter windows reduce stale ownership and make reporting cleaner.
- Escrow mediation: include a requirement that partner ops runs a 1:1 with partner AE and the Redwood AE within 5 business days.
- Evidence: OK with call/log evidence, but make it clear we accept CRM activity + signed mutual action plan items.

Operational asks:
- Add CS to the notification loop for accounts flagged as customer-risk if deals are past 60 days.
- Can you add a sample email template for the 7-day objection? I'll help draft that.

If we're aligned I can pilot this on three high-overlap accounts (Acme Cloud, NovaEdge, and Orbit Labs) next week.

Marissa

Thanks — quick operations POV. I reviewed claim-matrix-v1.xlsx and pushed a draft update to the shared drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcClaimMatrix (see file 'claim-matrix-v1_JW-edits.xlsx').

Key operational changes I'm proposing:
- Event-driven flags: partner_activity is any CRM task logged + external meeting invite accepted. seller_objection is a tagged note in the HS deal.
- Automation: when Escrowed set contact role to 'Partner Escrow' and create a tracked communication thread; if no activity after 21 days (configurable), run automated handback and log audit record.
- Handback ownership: default to 'owner_of_record' unless the seller has a documented motion and the partner signs a 1:1 remediation plan.
- Edge cases: reseller carve-outs — mark as 'Reseller Exempt' if reseller contract clause present (requires legal flag).

Operational checklist I can implement after final signoff:
- Update HS workflows and create the 'Partner Escrow' contact role.
- Add the 7-day objection email template (will draft).
- Add webhook to log evidence artifacts to drive reports.

I'll also add a small runbook for on-call partner-ops to handle contested claims.

— Jonas
